source.text: וַיְהִי֙ כְּכַלּ֣וֹת שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה לִבְנ֥וֹת אֶת־בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־חֵ֣שֶׁק שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָפֵ֖ץ לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when finished Solomon building the house of Yahweh and the house of the king and all [the] desire of Solomon which he delighted to do,

en.L: And it happened, when Solomon had finished building the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the house of the king, and all the desire of Solomon that he had been pleased to do,
en.B: After Solomon had completed the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the royal palace, and everything else he had set his heart on making,
en.R: Solomon finished building {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple and the royal palace. He also finished everything else he had wanted to build.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando Salomón terminó de edificar la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y la casa del rey, y todo lo que Salomón deseó y quiso hacer,
es.B: Cuando Salomón terminó la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y el palacio real, y todo lo demás que había deseado hacer,
es.R: Salomón terminó de construir el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y el palacio real. También terminó todo lo demás que había querido construir.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand Salomon eut achevé de bâtir la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et la maison du roi, et tout ce que Salomon désirait et qu’il lui plut de faire,
fr.B: Lorsque Salomon eut achevé la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et le palais royal, et tout ce qu’il avait eu à cœur de réaliser,
fr.R: Salomon a terminé la construction du temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et du palais royal. Il a aussi terminé tout ce qu’il avait voulu construire.

sw.L: Ikawa Sulemani alipomaliza kujenga nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na nyumba ya mfalme, na yote aliyoyatamani Sulemani aliyopendezwa kuyafanya,
sw.B: Baada ya Sulemani kumaliza nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na ikulu ya mfalme, na kila kitu kingine alichokuwa ameweka moyo wake kukifanya,
sw.R: Sulemani alimaliza kujenga hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na ikulu ya mfalme. Akamaliza pia kila kitu kingine alichotaka kujenga.

vi.L: Khi Sa-lô-môn đã xây xong nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và cung điện của vua, cùng mọi điều Sa-lô-môn ao ước và muốn làm,
vi.B: Sau khi Sa-lô-môn đã hoàn tất nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, cung điện của vua, và mọi công trình khác vua đã ước muốn thực hiện,
vi.R: Sa-lô-môn đã xây xong đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và cung điện của vua. Vua cũng hoàn tất mọi công trình khác vua muốn xây.

ko.L: 그리고 솔로몬이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집과 왕의 집과 솔로몬이 하고 싶어 하던 모든 것을 짓기를 마쳤을 때에,
ko.B: 솔로몬이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집과 왕궁과 그 밖에 짓고 싶어 하던 모든 것을 다 지었다.
ko.R: 솔로몬은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전과 왕궁을 다 지었다. 그리고 그 밖에 짓고 싶어 하던 것도 모두 지었다.

decisions.choice: when Solomon had finished: a time clause that leads into verse 2
decisions.reason: The verse sets the time for what follows; the main statement, that the LORD appeared to Solomon, comes in verse 2. Verse 10 puts the end of the building work twenty years after it began (6:38; 7:1).

decisions.choice: the desire of Solomon that he was pleased to do: every building project he longed to carry out
decisions.reason: The noun means something longed for or set one's heart on. Here it sums up the rest of Solomon's building, which verse 19 describes with the same word.

decisions.choice: the house of the king: Solomon's royal palace
decisions.reason: This is the palace complex described in 7:1-12, which took thirteen years to build.

decisions.choice: the royal palace (Balanced, Readable); the LORD's temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: "House" means a temple when it is God's and a palace when it is the king's. Balanced keeps "house" for God's house, as in chapter 3; Readable says "temple" there, and both say "royal palace" for the king's. Readable makes the verse a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: Verse 1 closed as a sentence at Balanced
alternatives: one sentence into verse 2, as Literal
decisions.reason: Korean puts the main verb last; closing the time clause keeps verse 2's event under its own number.

en.L: that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Solomon a second time, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had appeared to him at Gibeon.

en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to Solomon again, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had appeared to him at Gibeon.

es.B: {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se le apareció a Salomón por segunda vez, como se le había aparecido en Gabaón.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se le apareció otra vez a Salomón, tal como se le había aparecido en Gabaón.

fr.L: {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} apparut à Salomon une seconde fois, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui était apparu à Gabaon.
fr.B: {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} apparut à Salomon une seconde fois, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui était apparu à Gabaon.

sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimtokea Sulemani mara ya pili, kama alivyomtokea huko Gibeoni.
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamtokea Sulemani tena, kama alivyomtokea huko Gibeoni.

vi.B: thì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hiện ra với Sa-lô-môn lần thứ hai, như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã hiện ra với vua tại Ga-ba-ôn.
vi.R: Bấy giờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} lại hiện ra với Sa-lô-môn, như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã hiện ra với vua tại Ga-ba-ôn.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 기브온에서 솔로몬에게 나타나셨던 것처럼 두 번째로 그에게 나타나셨다.
ko.B: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 기브온에서 나타나셨던 것처럼 두 번째로 솔로몬에게 나타나셨다.
ko.R: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 기브온에서 나타나셨던 것처럼 다시 솔로몬에게 나타나셨다.

decisions.choice: a second time, as at Gibeon: a second meeting like the dream of 3:4-15
decisions.reason: The first time, at the start of his reign, the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream at Gibeon and offered him whatever he asked (3:5). The second appearance comes when his building is complete and answers his prayer at the dedication of the house (8:22-53).

decisions.choice: the second appearance follows the end of all the building
decisions.reason: Verse 1 ties this appearance to the completion of all Solomon's work, not only the temple. The text does not say how long after the dedication of chapter 8 it came.

decisions.choice: that
decisions.reason: Literal joins the verse to the "when" clause of verse 1 with "that", as the Hebrew "and it happened, when ... and" does.

decisions.choice: verse 1 runs into verse 2 without "que"
decisions.reason: The English Literal adds "that" to join the time clause of verse 1 to the main clause; Spanish needs no word for it, and the clause simply follows the comma.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו שָׁ֠מַעְתִּי אֶת־תְּפִלָּתְךָ֣ וְאֶת־תְּחִנָּתְךָ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִתְחַנַּ֣נְתָּה לְפָנַי֒ הִקְדַּ֗שְׁתִּי אֶת־הַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּנִ֔תָה לָשֽׂוּם־שְׁמִ֥י שָׁ֖ם עַד־עוֹלָ֑ם וְהָי֨וּ עֵינַ֧י וְלִבִּ֛י שָׁ֖ם כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to him, I have heard your prayer and your supplication which you have sought favor before me; I have consecrated the house this which you have built to put my name there until forever, and will be my eyes and my heart there all the days.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "I have heard your prayer and your plea for favor that you made before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I have consecrated this house that you have built, to put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name there forever; and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart will be there all the days.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "I have heard your prayer and the plea for mercy you made to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I have set apart as holy this house you have built, and I have put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name there forever. My eyes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart will always be there.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "I have heard your prayer. I have heard you ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for mercy. I have made this temple you built a holy place. I have chosen it to carry {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name forever. I will always watch over it and care for it.

es.L: Y le dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: «He oído tu oración y tu súplica que has hecho delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. He consagrado esta casa que has edificado, para poner allí {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre para siempre; y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} corazón estarán allí todos los días.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo: «He oído tu oración y la súplica que me hiciste. He apartado como santa esta casa que has edificado, y he puesto allí {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre para siempre. Mis ojos y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} corazón estarán siempre allí.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo: «He oído tu oración. Te he oído pedirme misericordia. He hecho de este templo que construiste un lugar santo. Lo he escogido para que lleve {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre para siempre. Siempre lo vigilaré y lo cuidaré.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui dit : « J’ai entendu ta prière et ta supplication, que tu as faite devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. J’ai consacré cette maison que tu as bâtie, pour y mettre {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom à jamais ; et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} yeux et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} cœur seront là tous les jours.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui dit : « J’ai entendu la prière et la supplication que tu m’as adressées. J’ai consacré cette maison que tu as bâtie, et j’y ai mis {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom pour toujours. Mes yeux et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} cœur y seront toujours.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a dit : « J’ai entendu ta prière. Je t’ai entendu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} demander pitié. J’ai fait de ce temple que tu as construit un lieu saint. Je l’ai choisi pour qu’il porte {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom pour toujours. Je veillerai toujours sur lui et j’en prendrai soin.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Nimesikia sala yako na dua yako ya kuomba fadhili uliyoiomba mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Nimeitakasa nyumba hii uliyoijenga, ili kuliweka jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} huko milele; na macho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na moyo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} vitakuwa huko siku zote.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Nimesikia sala yako na dua ya rehema uliyoniomba. Nimeiweka wakfu nyumba hii uliyoijenga, nami nimeliweka jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} huko milele. Macho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na moyo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} vitakuwa huko daima.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Nimesikia sala yako. Nimekusikia ukiniomba rehema. Nimelifanya hekalu hili ulilojenga kuwa mahali patakatifu. Nimelichagua liitwe kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} milele. Nitaliangalia na kulitunza daima.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với vua: "Ta đã nghe lời cầu nguyện và lời nài xin ơn mà ngươi đã dâng trước mặt Ta. Ta đã biệt riêng ra thánh nhà này mà ngươi đã xây, để đặt danh Ta ở đó đời đời; mắt Ta và lòng Ta sẽ ở đó mọi ngày.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với vua: "Ta đã nghe lời cầu nguyện và lời nài xin thương xót con đã dâng lên Ta. Ta đã biệt riêng ra thánh ngôi nhà con đã xây, và đã đặt danh Ta tại đó đời đời. Mắt Ta và lòng Ta sẽ luôn ở đó.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với vua: "Ta đã nghe lời cầu nguyện của con. Ta đã nghe con xin Ta thương xót. Ta đã làm cho đền thờ con xây thành nơi thánh. Ta đã chọn nơi ấy để mang danh Ta đời đời. Ta sẽ luôn trông nom và chăm sóc nơi ấy.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "네가 내 앞에서 은혜를 구한 네 기도와 네 간구를 내가 들었다. 네가 지은 이 집을 내가 거룩하게 구별하여 내 이름을 영원히 거기에 두었다. 그리고 내 눈과 내 마음이 언제나 거기에 있을 것이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "네가 내 앞에서 드린 기도와 자비를 구한 간구를 내가 들었다. 나는 네가 지은 이 집을 거룩하게 구별하여 내 이름을 영원히 그곳에 두었다. 내 눈과 내 마음이 언제나 그곳에 있을 것이다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "나는 네 기도를 들었다. 네가 나에게 자비를 구하는 것을 들었다. 나는 네가 지은 이 성전을 거룩한 곳으로 삼았다. 이곳을 택하여 영원히 내 이름을 두었다. 나는 언제나 이곳을 지켜보며 돌볼 것이다.

decisions.choice: I have heard your prayer: the answer to Solomon's prayer at the dedication
decisions.reason: Solomon had asked the LORD to hear the prayers made at this house and to keep his eyes open toward it night and day (8:28-30, 52). This is the reply, and the warning that follows in verses 6-9 echoes the disasters his prayer had named (8:33-34, 46-50).

decisions.choice: to put my name there: to claim the house as his own and make it the place where he is known and called on
decisions.reason: The "name" stands for the LORD himself as he makes himself known. Deuteronomy speaks of the place the LORD would choose "to put his name there" (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11), and Solomon used the same language (8:16, 29). The LORD's presence is not confined there (8:27), but this is where his name is honored.

decisions.choice: my eyes and my heart will be there: the LORD's constant attention and care
decisions.reason: Eyes stand for watching over something, and the heart for one's concern and will. "All the days" means always, without a break.

decisions.choice: consecrated: made holy, set apart for the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something holy, that is, set apart as belonging to God. The LORD himself now does what the dedication ceremony had asked for.

decisions.choice: I have chosen it to carry my name ... I will always watch over it and care for it
decisions.reason: Readable explains both pictures instead of reproducing them: putting the name becomes choosing the house to carry his name, and eyes and heart become watching over and caring for it.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֞ה אִם־תֵּלֵ֣ךְ לְפָנַ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר הָלַ֜ךְ דָּוִ֤ד אָבִ֨יךָ֙ בְּתָם־לֵבָ֣ב וּבְיֹ֔שֶׁר לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֑יךָ חֻקַּ֥י וּמִשְׁפָּטַ֖י תִּשְׁמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, if you will walk before me as walked David your father in integrity of heart and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded you; my statutes and my judgments you will keep,

en.L: And you, if you walk before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as David your father walked, in integrity of heart and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded you, [and] keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments,
en.B: As for you, if you live before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as your father David did, with a whole heart and with uprightness, doing everything I have commanded you and keeping {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings,
en.R: Now you must live faithfully before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, as your father David did. Your heart must be sincere and honest. Do everything I have commanded you, and obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and rules.

es.L: Y tú, si andas delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} como anduvo David tu padre, con integridad de corazón y con rectitud, haciendo conforme a todo lo que te he mandado, [y] guardas {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} estatutos y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} decretos,
es.B: En cuanto a ti, si vives delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} como lo hizo tu padre David, con un corazón íntegro y con rectitud, haciendo todo lo que te he mandado y guardando {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} estatutos y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} normas,
es.R: Ahora tú debes vivir fielmente delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, como lo hizo tu padre David. Tu corazón debe ser sincero y honrado. Haz todo lo que te he mandado, y obedece {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} leyes y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} normas.

fr.L: Et toi, si tu marches devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} comme a marché David ton père, avec intégrité de cœur et avec droiture, pour faire selon tout ce que je t’ai commandé, [et] si tu gardes {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} prescriptions et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} jugements,
fr.B: Quant à toi, si tu vis devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} comme l’a fait ton père David, d’un cœur intègre et avec droiture, en faisant tout ce que je t’ai commandé et en gardant {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} prescriptions et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} règles,
fr.R: Maintenant, tu dois vivre fidèlement devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, comme ton père David. Ton cœur doit être sincère et honnête. Fais tout ce que je t’ai commandé, et obéis à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} lois et à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} règles.

sw.L: Nawe, ukienda mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kama Daudi baba yako alivyokwenda, kwa ukamilifu wa moyo na kwa unyofu, kutenda sawasawa na yote niliyokuamuru, [na] kushika kanuni {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} na hukumu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}},
sw.B: Na wewe, ukiishi mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kama baba yako Daudi alivyoishi, kwa moyo mkamilifu na kwa unyofu, ukitenda yote niliyokuamuru na kushika kanuni {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} na maamuzi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}},
sw.R: Sasa wewe lazima uishi kwa uaminifu mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, kama baba yako Daudi alivyofanya. Moyo wako lazima uwe safi na mnyofu. Fanya yote niliyokuamuru, na utii sheria {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} na kanuni {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}.

vi.L: Còn ngươi, nếu ngươi bước đi trước mặt Ta như Đa-vít cha ngươi đã bước đi, với tấm lòng trọn vẹn và ngay thẳng, làm theo mọi điều Ta đã truyền cho ngươi, [và] giữ các luật lệ và phán quyết của Ta,
vi.B: Còn con, nếu con sống trước mặt Ta như Đa-vít cha con đã sống, với lòng trọn vẹn và ngay thẳng, làm mọi điều Ta truyền cho con, giữ các luật lệ và phán quyết của Ta,
vi.R: Bây giờ con phải sống trung tín trước mặt Ta như Đa-vít cha con đã sống. Lòng con phải chân thành và ngay thẳng. Hãy làm mọi điều Ta đã truyền cho con, và vâng giữ các luật lệ và phán quyết của Ta.

ko.L: 그리고 너는, 만일 네 아버지 다윗이 걸었던 것처럼 마음을 온전하게 하고 정직하게 내 앞에서 걸어, 내가 너에게 명령한 모든 것대로 행하고 내 규례와 내 법도를 지키면,
ko.B: 너는 네 아버지 다윗처럼 온전한 마음과 정직함으로 내 앞에서 살아라. 내가 너에게 명령한 모든 것을 행하고 내 규례와 법도를 지켜라.
ko.R: 이제 너는 네 아버지 다윗처럼 내 앞에서 신실하게 살아야 한다. 네 마음은 진실하고 정직해야 한다. 내가 너에게 명령한 것을 모두 지키고, 내 법과 규칙을 따라야 한다.

decisions.choice: walk before me: live one's whole life in the LORD's sight and service
decisions.reason: The same picture is used of Abraham (Genesis 17:1) and of David (3:6), and in David's charge to Solomon (2:4).

decisions.choice: integrity of heart and uprightness: an undivided and honest heart
decisions.reason: The first noun means completeness or wholeness: a heart not split between the LORD and anything else. The second means straightness, doing what is right. Solomon's heart later fails exactly here (11:4).

decisions.choice: if ...: the condition on which the promise of verse 5 depends
decisions.reason: The verse is the first half of a conditional sentence; verse 5 gives the result. The LORD's promise to Solomon's line depends on his obedience, as 2:4 and 8:25 had already said.

decisions.choice: statutes and rulings (Balanced); laws and rules (Readable)
decisions.reason: These follow the book-wide wording for this pair of terms.

decisions.choice: you must ... (verse 5: If you do)
decisions.reason: Readable states the conditions as plain sentences and gives the "if" at the start of verse 5, as it does in 2:4. The meaning is the same: the promise depends on these conditions.

decisions.choice: The condition of verse 4 given as commands at Balanced
decisions.reason: Closing verse 4 as its own sentence keeps the promise of verse 5 under its number; verse 5 opens with "그러면", as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַהֲקִ֨מֹתִ֜י אֶת־כִּסֵּ֧א מַֽמְלַכְתְּךָ֛ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְעֹלָ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבַּ֗רְתִּי עַל־דָּוִ֤ד אָבִ֨יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֤ת לְךָ֙ אִ֔ישׁ מֵעַ֖ל כִּסֵּ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: then I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, as I spoke concerning David your father, saying, Not will be cut off for you a man from on [the] throne of Israel.

en.L: then I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, as I spoke concerning David your father, saying, 'A man will not be cut off for you from on the throne of Israel.'
en.B: then I will make the throne of your kingdom over Israel secure forever, as I promised your father David when I said, 'There will always be a man of your line on the throne of Israel.'
en.R: If you do, I will make sure that your family rules over Israel forever. That is what I promised your father David. I told him, 'One of your family will always sit on Israel's throne.'

es.L: yo afirmaré el trono de tu reino sobre Israel para siempre, como hablé a David tu padre, diciendo: ‘No te faltará varón sobre el trono de Israel’.
es.B: yo afirmaré para siempre el trono de tu reino sobre Israel, como se lo prometí a tu padre David cuando le dije: ‘Siempre habrá un hombre de tu linaje en el trono de Israel’.
es.R: Si lo haces, me aseguraré de que tu familia reine sobre Israel para siempre. Eso es lo que le prometí a tu padre David. Le dije: ‘Siempre habrá uno de tu familia sentado en el trono de Israel’.

fr.L: alors j’affermirai le trône de ta royauté sur Israël à jamais, comme je l’ai dit à David ton père, disant : “Il ne te sera pas retranché un homme de dessus le trône d’Israël.”
fr.B: alors j’affermirai pour toujours le trône de ta royauté sur Israël, comme je l’ai promis à ton père David quand j’ai dit : “Il y aura toujours un homme de ta lignée sur le trône d’Israël.”
fr.R: Si tu le fais, je ferai en sorte que ta famille règne sur Israël pour toujours. C’est ce que j’ai promis à ton père David. Je lui ai dit : “Il y aura toujours quelqu’un de ta famille sur le trône d’Israël.”

sw.L: ndipo nitakithibitisha kiti cha enzi cha ufalme wako juu ya Israeli milele, kama nilivyomwambia Daudi baba yako, nikisema, 'Hutakosa mtu juu ya kiti cha enzi cha Israeli.'
sw.B: ndipo nitakiimarisha kiti cha enzi cha ufalme wako juu ya Israeli milele, kama nilivyomwahidi baba yako Daudi niliposema, 'Daima kutakuwa na mtu wa ukoo wako juu ya kiti cha enzi cha Israeli.'
sw.R: Ukifanya hivyo, nitahakikisha kwamba jamaa yako inatawala Israeli milele. Hivyo ndivyo nilivyomwahidi baba yako Daudi. Nilimwambia, 'Mtu wa jamaa yako ataketi daima juu ya kiti cha enzi cha Israeli.'

vi.L: thì Ta sẽ làm vững ngai vương quốc ngươi trên Y-sơ-ra-ên đời đời, như Ta đã phán về Đa-vít cha ngươi rằng: 'Ngươi sẽ không bao giờ thiếu người ngồi trên ngai Y-sơ-ra-ên.'
vi.B: thì Ta sẽ làm cho ngai vương quốc của con trên Y-sơ-ra-ên được vững bền đời đời, như Ta đã hứa với Đa-vít cha con: 'Dòng dõi con sẽ luôn có người ngồi trên ngai Y-sơ-ra-ên.'
vi.R: Nếu con làm như vậy, Ta sẽ cho dòng dõi con cai trị Y-sơ-ra-ên mãi mãi. Đó là điều Ta đã hứa với Đa-vít cha con. Ta đã phán với người: 'Gia đình con sẽ luôn có người ngồi trên ngai Y-sơ-ra-ên.'

ko.L: 내가 네 아버지 다윗에게 '이스라엘의 왕좌에서 네게 [대를 이을] 사람이 끊어지지 않을 것이다' 하고 말한 대로, 이스라엘을 다스리는 네 왕위를 영원히 굳게 세울 것이다.
ko.B: 그러면 내가 네 아버지 다윗에게 '이스라엘의 왕좌에 오를 사람이 네 집안에서 끊어지지 않을 것이다' 하고 약속한 대로, 이스라엘을 다스리는 네 왕위를 영원히 든든하게 세워 주겠다.
ko.R: 그렇게 하면 나는 네 집안이 영원히 이스라엘을 다스리게 하겠다. 그것은 내가 네 아버지 다윗에게 약속한 것이다. 나는 그에게 '네 집안에서 언제나 이스라엘의 왕이 나올 것이다' 하고 말했다.

decisions.choice: as I spoke concerning David your father: the promise of 2 Samuel 7
decisions.reason: The LORD promised David through Nathan that his throne would stand forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16). David passed it on to Solomon with its condition (2:4), and Solomon recalled it in his prayer (8:25).

decisions.choice: a man will not be cut off for you from the throne: you will never lack a descendant on the throne
decisions.reason: "Cut off" means removed or brought to an end. The promise is that David's line will never be without a king of his own family on Israel's throne.

decisions.choice: wording of 2:4 reused
decisions.reason: The promise is the same as in 2:4, so each level repeats the wording it uses there.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2:4 reused
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): the promise keeps the Spanish wording of 2:4 at each level.

decisions.choice: wording of 2:4 reused
decisions.reason: The promise is the same as in 2:4, so each Swahili level repeats the wording it uses there.

source.text: אִם־שׁ֨וֹב תְּשֻׁב֜וּן אַתֶּ֤ם וּבְנֵיכֶם֙ מֵֽאַחֲרַ֔י וְלֹ֤א תִשְׁמְרוּ֙ מִצְוֺתַ֣י חֻקֹּתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִפְנֵיכֶ֑ם וַהֲלַכְתֶּ֗ם וַעֲבַדְתֶּם֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֖ם לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: If turning you turn back, you and your sons, from after me, and not you keep my commandments, my statutes, which I have set before you, and you go and serve gods other and bow down to them,

en.L: [But] if you indeed turn back, you or your {{gender:children|sons}}, from [following] after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and do not keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, that I have set before you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them,
en.B: But if you or your descendants turn away from following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and do not keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes that I have set before you, and instead go off to serve other gods and bow down to them,
en.R: But suppose you or your descendants turn away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Suppose you do not obey the commands and laws I have given you, but you go and serve other gods and worship them.

es.L: [Pero] si de veras se apartan de en pos de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{plural_you:ustedes o sus hijos, y no guardan|vosotros o vuestros hijos, y no guardáis}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} mandamientos y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} estatutos que he puesto delante de {{plural_you:ustedes, y van y sirven|vosotros, y vais y servís}} a otros dioses y se postran ante ellos,
es.B: Pero si {{plural_you:ustedes o sus descendientes se apartan|vosotros o vuestros descendientes os apartáis}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y no {{plural_you:guardan|guardáis}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} mandamientos y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} estatutos que he puesto delante de {{plural_you:ustedes, y en cambio van a servir a otros dioses y se postran|vosotros, y en cambio vais a servir a otros dioses y os postráis}} ante ellos,
es.R: Pero supongamos que {{plural_you:ustedes o sus descendientes se apartan|vosotros o vuestros descendientes os apartáis}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Supongamos que no {{plural_you:obedecen|obedecéis}} los mandamientos y leyes que {{plural_you:les|os}} he dado, sino que {{plural_you:van y sirven|vais y servís}} a otros dioses y los {{plural_you:adoran|adoráis}}.

fr.L: [Mais] si vous vous détournez, vous et vos {{gender:enfants|fils}}, de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} suivre, et si vous ne gardez pas {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} commandements, {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} prescriptions, que j’ai mis devant vous, et si vous allez servir d’autres dieux et vous prosterner devant eux,
fr.B: Mais si vous vous détournez de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, vous ou vos descendants, si vous ne gardez pas les commandements et les prescriptions que j’ai mis devant vous, et si vous allez servir d’autres dieux et vous prosterner devant eux,
fr.R: Mais supposons que toi ou tes descendants, vous vous détourniez de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Supposons que vous n’obéissiez pas aux commandements et aux lois que je vous ai donnés, mais que vous alliez servir d’autres dieux et les adorer.

sw.L: [Lakini] mkigeuka kweli, ninyi au wana wenu, msinifuate {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, wala msizishike amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, kanuni {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}, nilizoweka mbele yenu, mkaenda na kuitumikia miungu mingine na kuisujudia,
sw.B: Lakini ninyi au wazao wenu mkigeuka na kuacha kunifuata, wala msizishike amri {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} na kanuni {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} nilizoweka mbele yenu, badala yake mkaenda kuitumikia miungu mingine na kuisujudia,
sw.R: Lakini tuseme ninyi au wazao wenu mnageuka mkaniacha. Tuseme hamtii amri na sheria nilizowapa, bali mnaenda kuitumikia miungu mingine na kuiabudu.

vi.L: [Nhưng] nếu các ngươi, ngươi hay con cái ngươi, quay lưng không theo Ta, không giữ các điều răn và luật lệ Ta đã đặt trước mặt các ngươi, mà đi phục vụ các thần khác và quỳ lạy chúng,
vi.B: Nhưng nếu con hay con cháu con quay lưng không theo Ta, không giữ các điều răn và luật lệ Ta đã đặt trước mặt các con, mà đi phục vụ các thần khác và quỳ lạy chúng,
vi.R: Nhưng giả sử con hay con cháu con quay lưng lìa bỏ Ta. Giả sử các con không vâng giữ các điều răn và luật lệ Ta đã ban cho các con, mà đi phục vụ và thờ lạy các thần khác.

ko.L: [그러나] 만일 너희나 너희 자손이 나를 따르지 않고 돌아서서, 내가 너희 앞에 둔 내 계명과 내 규례를 지키지 않고, 가서 다른 신들을 섬기고 그들에게 절하면,
ko.B: 그러나 만일 너희나 너희 자손이 나를 따르지 않고 돌아서서, 내가 너희에게 준 계명과 규례를 지키지 않고 다른 신들을 섬기며 그들에게 절하면,
ko.R: 그러나 너희나 너희 자손이 나에게서 돌아선다고 하자. 내가 너희에게 준 명령과 법을 지키지 않고, 다른 신들을 섬기며 그들에게 절한다고 하자.

decisions.choice: you or your sons: the address widens from Solomon to his line and the people
decisions.reason: From here to verse 9 every "you" is plural, while verses 3-5 spoke to Solomon alone. The warning now covers Solomon, the kings after him and, as verse 7 shows, all Israel.

decisions.choice: if you indeed turn back: an emphatic form
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled, a way of stressing it: if you do turn away. It makes the warning firm, not tentative.

decisions.choice: serve other gods and bow down to them: breaking the first demand of the covenant
decisions.reason: Worshiping other gods breaks the first two commandments (Exodus 20:3-5) and is the sin that Deuteronomy says would bring exile (Deuteronomy 29:25-27).

decisions.choice: your children (Literal, with "sons" as the setting); your descendants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Sons" here means the generations after Solomon, so Balanced and Readable say "descendants".

decisions.choice: But suppose ...
decisions.reason: Readable states the conditions as their own sentences and gives the result in verse 7 with "then".

decisions.choice: plural_you spans from here to verse 9
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" turns plural here, taking in Solomon's sons and the people (m1); Spanish marks every plural "you" with the plural_you span. "hijos" (L) and "descendientes" (B, R) take no gender span.

decisions.choice: vous
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns to the plural here, Solomon and his line with him, so French moves from "tu" to "vous".

decisions.choice: ninyi (plural you)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "you" turns plural here (Solomon and his sons, then Israel), and Swahili marks this with "ninyi" and the verb prefix "m-", where English cannot show it.

decisions.choice: "con cái ngươi" (L); "con cháu con" (B, R) with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "con cái" and "con cháu" include sons and daughters, so the English setting has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: "너희" from verse 6, where the Hebrew "you" becomes plural
decisions.reason: God turns from Solomon alone to Solomon, his line and the people; Korean shows the plural, which English cannot.

source.text: וְהִכְרַתִּ֣י אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מֵעַ֨ל פְּנֵ֤י הָאֲדָמָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָתַ֣תִּי לָהֶ֔ם וְאֶת־הַבַּ֨יִת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִקְדַּ֣שְׁתִּי לִשְׁמִ֔י אֲשַׁלַּ֖ח מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑י וְהָיָ֧ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל לְמָשָׁ֥ל וְלִשְׁנִינָ֖ה בְּכָל־הָעַמִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: then I will cut off Israel from on [the] face of the ground which I have given to them, and the house which I have consecrated for my name I will send away from on my face; and will be Israel for a proverb and for a taunt among all the peoples.

en.L: then I will cut off Israel from the face of the land that I have given them; and the house that I have consecrated for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name I will send away from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence; and Israel will become a proverb and a byword among all the peoples.
en.B: then I will cut Israel off from the land I have given them, and I will cast this house that I have made holy for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight. Israel will become a proverb and a byword among all the peoples.
en.R: Then I will remove Israel from the land I gave them. I will reject this temple that I made holy for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and I will turn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face away from it. People of every nation will tell of what happened to Israel as a warning, and they will make fun of it.

es.L: entonces cortaré a Israel de sobre la faz de la tierra que les he dado; y la casa que he consagrado a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre la echaré de delante de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} rostro; e Israel será refrán y burla entre todos los pueblos.
es.B: entonces arrancaré a Israel de la tierra que les he dado, y echaré de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} presencia esta casa que he consagrado a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre. Israel será objeto de refranes y de burla entre todos los pueblos.
es.R: Entonces quitaré a Israel de la tierra que les di. Rechazaré este templo que hice santo para {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, y le daré la espalda. La gente de todas las naciones contará lo que le pasó a Israel como advertencia, y se burlará de él.

fr.L: alors je retrancherai Israël de la face du pays que je leur ai donné ; et la maison que j’ai consacrée à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, je la rejetterai loin de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} face ; et Israël deviendra un proverbe et une moquerie parmi tous les peuples.
fr.B: alors je retrancherai Israël du pays que je lui ai donné, et je rejetterai loin de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} face cette maison que j’ai consacrée à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom. Israël deviendra un sujet de proverbe et de moquerie parmi tous les peuples.
fr.R: Alors j’enlèverai Israël du pays que je lui ai donné. Je rejetterai ce temple que j’ai consacré à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, et je m’en détournerai. Dans toutes les nations, on racontera ce qui est arrivé à Israël pour servir d’avertissement, et on se moquera de lui.

sw.L: ndipo nitawakatilia mbali Israeli kutoka katika uso wa nchi niliyowapa; na nyumba niliyoitakasa kwa ajili ya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} nitaiondoa mbele za uso {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}; na Israeli watakuwa mithali na dhihaka kati ya mataifa yote.
sw.B: ndipo nitawakatilia mbali Israeli kutoka katika nchi niliyowapa, na nyumba hii niliyoiweka wakfu kwa ajili ya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} nitaitupa mbali na macho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Israeli watakuwa mithali na kitu cha dhihaka kati ya mataifa yote.
sw.R: Ndipo nitawaondoa Israeli katika nchi niliyowapa. Nitalikataa hekalu hili nililolifanya takatifu kwa ajili ya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, nami nitaugeuza uso {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mbali nalo. Watu wa kila taifa watasimulia yaliyowapata Israeli kuwa onyo, nao watawadhihaki.

vi.L: thì Ta sẽ diệt trừ Y-sơ-ra-ên khỏi mặt đất mà Ta đã ban cho họ; còn nhà mà Ta đã biệt riêng ra thánh cho danh Ta, Ta sẽ đuổi khỏi mặt Ta; và Y-sơ-ra-ên sẽ thành câu tục ngữ và lời chế giễu giữa mọi dân.
vi.B: thì Ta sẽ diệt trừ Y-sơ-ra-ên khỏi đất Ta đã ban cho họ, và Ta sẽ loại bỏ khỏi mắt Ta ngôi nhà Ta đã biệt riêng ra thánh cho danh Ta. Y-sơ-ra-ên sẽ trở thành câu tục ngữ và lời chế giễu giữa mọi dân.
vi.R: Bấy giờ Ta sẽ đuổi Y-sơ-ra-ên khỏi đất Ta đã ban cho họ. Ta sẽ từ bỏ đền thờ Ta đã biệt riêng ra thánh cho danh Ta, và Ta sẽ quay mặt khỏi nó. Dân mọi nước sẽ kể chuyện Y-sơ-ra-ên làm lời răn đe, và họ sẽ chế nhạo Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 내가 이스라엘에게 준 땅의 표면에서 이스라엘을 끊어 버릴 것이고, 내 이름을 위하여 거룩하게 구별한 이 집을 내 앞에서 내쫓을 것이다. 그리고 이스라엘은 모든 백성 가운데서 속담거리와 조롱거리가 될 것이다.
ko.B: 나는 이스라엘에게 준 땅에서 이스라엘을 끊어 버리고, 내 이름을 위하여 거룩하게 구별한 이 집을 내 앞에서 쫓아낼 것이다. 이스라엘은 모든 민족 가운데서 속담거리와 조롱거리가 될 것이다.
ko.R: 그러면 나는 이스라엘을 내가 준 땅에서 없애 버릴 것이다. 내 이름을 위하여 거룩하게 구별한 이 성전도 버리고 다시는 돌아보지 않을 것이다. 모든 나라 사람들이 이스라엘에게 일어난 일을 경고로 삼아 이야기하며 비웃을 것이다.

decisions.choice: cut off Israel from the face of the land: remove the people from their land
decisions.reason: The threat is exile, as the covenant curses warned (Deuteronomy 28:63-64). The book ends with it happening to Israel (2 Kings 17:23) and to Judah (2 Kings 25:21).

decisions.choice: send away from my presence: reject and cast off
decisions.reason: The verb is used of sending someone away for good. The house the LORD has just made holy will be cast out of his sight, as Jeremiah later warned (Jeremiah 7:14-15).

decisions.choice: a proverb and a byword: a saying about Israel's fate and a sharp taunt
decisions.reason: The first word is a saying people quote, here an example of disaster; the second is a cutting word of mockery. The same pair appears in the covenant curses (Deuteronomy 28:37).

decisions.choice: I will turn my face away from it; tell of what happened to Israel as a warning, and make fun of it
decisions.reason: Readable explains "send away from my face" and the two nouns, which have no simple plain-English equivalents.

source.text: וְהַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה עֶלְי֔וֹן כָּל־עֹבֵ֥ר עָלָ֖יו יִשֹּׁ֣ם וְשָׁרָ֑ק וְאָמְר֗וּ עַל־מֶ֨ה עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ כָּ֔כָה לָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את וְלַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the house this will be high; every [one] passing by it will be appalled and will hiss, and they will say, For what did Yahweh do thus to the land this and to the house this?

en.L: And [as for] this house, [which] will be high, everyone passing by it will be appalled and will hiss; and they will say, 'Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} done thus to this land and to this house?'
en.B: And this house, high as it stands, will leave everyone who passes by it appalled. They will hiss and ask, 'Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} dealt like this with this land and this house?'
en.R: This temple stands high and grand now, but everyone who passes by it will be shocked. They will hiss in horror and ask, 'Why has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} done this to the land and to this temple?'

es.L: Y esta casa, [que] será excelsa, todo el que pase junto a ella se asombrará y silbará, y dirán: ‘¿Por qué ha hecho así {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a esta tierra y a esta casa?’.
es.B: Y esta casa, por alta que esté, dejará espantado a todo el que pase junto a ella. Silbarán y preguntarán: ‘¿Por qué ha tratado así {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a esta tierra y a esta casa?’.
es.R: Este templo ahora se levanta alto y grandioso, pero todo el que pase junto a él se quedará espantado. Silbarán de horror y preguntarán: ‘¿Por qué {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le ha hecho esto a la tierra y a este templo?’.

fr.L: Et cette maison, [qui] sera élevée, quiconque passera près d’elle sera stupéfait et sifflera ; et l’on dira : “Pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a-t-il fait ainsi à ce pays et à cette maison ?”
fr.B: Et cette maison, si élevée soit-elle, laissera stupéfaits tous ceux qui passeront près d’elle. Ils siffleront et demanderont : “Pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a-t-il traité ainsi ce pays et cette maison ?”
fr.R: Ce temple est maintenant haut et magnifique, mais tous ceux qui passeront près de lui seront bouleversés. Ils siffleront d’horreur et demanderont : “Pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a-t-il fait cela à ce pays et à ce temple ?”

sw.L: Na nyumba hii, [iliyo] juu, kila apitaye karibu nayo atashangaa na kuzomea; nao watasema, 'Kwa nini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameitendea hivi nchi hii na nyumba hii?'
sw.B: Na nyumba hii, ijapokuwa sasa imeinuka juu, kila apitaye karibu nayo atashangaa. Watazomea na kuuliza, 'Kwa nini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameitendea hivi nchi hii na nyumba hii?'
sw.R: Hekalu hili sasa limesimama juu kwa fahari, lakini kila apitaye karibu nalo atashtuka. Watazomea kwa hofu na kuuliza, 'Kwa nini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameitendea nchi hii na hekalu hili mambo haya?'

vi.L: Còn nhà này, [vốn] cao vút, mọi người đi ngang qua sẽ kinh ngạc và huýt gió; họ sẽ nói: 'Tại sao {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã làm như vậy cho xứ này và cho nhà này?'
vi.B: Ngôi nhà này dù cao vút bây giờ, ai đi ngang qua cũng sẽ kinh hoàng. Họ sẽ huýt gió và hỏi: 'Tại sao {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã đối xử như vậy với xứ này và nhà này?'
vi.R: Đền thờ này bây giờ cao lớn và tráng lệ, nhưng ai đi ngang qua cũng sẽ sửng sốt. Họ sẽ huýt gió kinh hãi và hỏi: 'Tại sao {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã làm như vậy cho xứ này và cho đền thờ này?'

ko.L: 그리고 이 집은 높겠지만, 그 곁을 지나가는 사람마다 놀라며 쉿 소리를 내고 '어찌하여 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 땅과 이 집에 이렇게 하셨는가?' 하고 말할 것이다.
ko.B: 지금은 이 집이 높이 솟아 있지만, 그 곁을 지나가는 사람마다 놀라 혀를 차며 '어찌하여 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 땅과 이 집을 이렇게 하셨는가?' 하고 물을 것이다.
ko.R: 지금은 이 성전이 높고 웅장하지만, 그 곁을 지나가는 사람마다 깜짝 놀랄 것이다. 그들은 끔찍해서 혀를 차며 '어찌하여 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 땅과 이 성전을 이렇게 하셨는가?' 하고 물을 것이다.

decisions.choice: will be high: read as "though it is now lofty"
alternatives: will become a heap of ruins
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says this house "will be high" (or "most high"), which is hard to fit with the ruin the verse describes. Taken as it stands, it means: lofty as this house is, everyone will be appalled at it. The parallel in 2 Chronicles 7:21 reads "which was exalted". Some early translations read "will become a heap of ruins", which may reflect a different Hebrew word (compare Micah 3:12).

decisions.choice: appalled and will hiss: shock and scorn at a ruin
decisions.reason: Hissing or whistling was a gesture of horror and mockery at a place struck by disaster (Jeremiah 19:8; 49:17; Lamentations 2:15-16).

decisions.choice: why has the LORD done thus to this land: the question of Deuteronomy 29
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy foresees the nations asking the same question about the ruined land and gives the same answer (Deuteronomy 29:23-25; compare Jeremiah 22:8-9).

decisions.choice: high as it stands (Balanced); stands high and grand now, but (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the contrast explicit, since "this house will be high" alone would sound like a promise.

decisions.choice: hiss
decisions.reason: "Hiss" keeps the sound of the gesture; Readable adds "in horror" so it is not taken as anger.

decisions.choice: "silbará" / "silbarán"
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): hissing is a sound of horror and scorn at a ruin; Spanish keeps "silbar" at every level, and Readable adds "de horror".

decisions.choice: "huýt gió"
decisions.reason: The hiss of horror at a ruin (meaning decision); Vietnamese "huýt gió" keeps the sound, and Readable adds "kinh hãi", as the English says "in horror".

decisions.choice: "혀를 차며" (B, R); "쉿 소리를 내고" (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew hiss is a sound of scorn and horror; Korean expresses the same with 혀를 차다, while Literal keeps the sound.

source.text: וְאָמְר֗וּ עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָזְב֜וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹצִ֣יא אֶת־אֲבֹתָם֮ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ וַֽיַּחֲזִ֨קוּ֙ בֵּאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲו֥וּלָהֶ֖ם וַיַּעַבְדֻ֑ם עַל־כֵּ֗ן הֵבִ֤יא יְהוָה֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֥ת כָּל־הָרָעָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And they will say, Because that they forsook Yahweh their God who brought out their fathers from [the] land of Egypt, and they took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them; therefore has brought Yahweh on them all the disaster this.

en.L: And they will say, 'Because they forsook {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and they took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them; therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought on them all this disaster.'"
en.B: And people will answer, 'Because they abandoned {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, who brought their ancestors out of the land of Egypt, and they embraced other gods and worshiped and served them. That is why {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought all this disaster on them.'"
en.R: And people will answer, 'It is because they left {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, who brought their ancestors out of Egypt. They held on to other gods and worshiped and served them. That is why {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought all this trouble on them.'"

es.L: Y dirán: ‘Porque abandonaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} su Dios, que sacó a sus padres de la tierra de Egipto, y se aferraron a otros dioses y se postraron ante ellos y los sirvieron; por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha traído sobre ellos todo este mal’».
es.B: Y la gente responderá: ‘Porque abandonaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} su Dios, que sacó a sus antepasados de la tierra de Egipto, y se aferraron a otros dioses, los adoraron y los sirvieron. Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha traído sobre ellos toda esta desgracia’».
es.R: Y la gente responderá: ‘Es porque dejaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} su Dios, que sacó a sus antepasados de Egipto. Se aferraron a otros dioses, los adoraron y les sirvieron. Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha traído sobre ellos todos estos males’».

fr.L: Et l’on dira : “Parce qu’ils ont abandonné {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur Dieu, qui avait fait sortir leurs pères du pays d’Égypte, et qu’ils se sont attachés à d’autres dieux, se sont prosternés devant eux et les ont servis ; c’est pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait venir sur eux tout ce malheur.” »
fr.B: Et on répondra : “Parce qu’ils ont abandonné {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur Dieu, qui avait fait sortir leurs ancêtres du pays d’Égypte, et qu’ils se sont attachés à d’autres dieux, se sont prosternés devant eux et les ont servis. Voilà pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait venir sur eux tout ce malheur.” »
fr.R: Et on répondra : “C’est parce qu’ils ont abandonné {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur Dieu, qui avait fait sortir leurs ancêtres d’Égypte. Ils se sont attachés à d’autres dieux, ils les ont adorés et servis. C’est pour cela que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait venir tous ces malheurs sur eux.” »

sw.L: Nao watasema, 'Kwa sababu walimwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wao, aliyewatoa baba zao katika nchi ya Misri, wakashikamana na miungu mingine, wakaisujudia na kuitumikia; ndiyo maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameleta juu yao maafa haya yote.'"
sw.B: Na watu watajibu, 'Ni kwa sababu walimwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wao, aliyewatoa babu zao katika nchi ya Misri, wakaikumbatia miungu mingine, wakaiabudu na kuitumikia. Ndiyo sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameleta juu yao maafa haya yote.'"
sw.R: Na watu watajibu, 'Ni kwa sababu walimwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wao, aliyewatoa babu zao Misri. Wakashikamana na miungu mingine, wakaiabudu na kuitumikia. Ndiyo sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameleta taabu hizi zote juu yao.'"

vi.L: Người ta sẽ đáp: 'Vì họ đã lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của họ, là Đấng đã đem tổ phụ họ ra khỏi xứ Ai Cập, mà bám lấy các thần khác, quỳ lạy và phục vụ các thần ấy; vì thế {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giáng trên họ tất cả tai họa này.'"
vi.B: Người ta sẽ đáp: 'Vì họ đã lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của họ, là Đấng đã đem tổ tiên họ ra khỏi xứ Ai Cập, mà đi theo các thần khác, thờ lạy và phục vụ các thần ấy. Vì vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giáng trên họ tất cả tai họa này.'"
vi.R: Người ta sẽ trả lời: 'Ấy là vì họ đã lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của họ, là Đấng đã đem tổ tiên họ ra khỏi Ai Cập. Họ đã bám lấy các thần khác, thờ lạy và phục vụ các thần ấy. Vì vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giáng trên họ mọi tai họa này.'"

ko.L: 그러면 사람들이 '그들이 자기 조상들을 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 내신 자기 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버리고, 다른 신들을 붙잡아 그들에게 절하고 그들을 섬겼기 때문이다. 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 모든 재앙을 그들에게 내리셨다' 하고 말할 것이다."
ko.B: 그러면 사람들이 대답할 것이다. '그들이 자기 조상들을 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 내신 자기 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버리고, 다른 신들을 받아들여 그들에게 절하고 그들을 섬겼기 때문이다. 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 모든 재앙을 그들에게 내리셨다.'"
ko.R: 그러면 사람들이 대답할 것이다. '그것은 그들이 자기 조상들을 이집트에서 이끌어 내신 자기 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 떠났기 때문이다. 그들은 다른 신들을 붙들고 그들에게 절하며 섬겼다. 그래서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 모든 재앙을 그들에게 내리셨다.'"

decisions.choice: they will say ... they forsook: the onlookers answer, and "they" are the people of Israel
decisions.reason: The same passers-by of verse 8 give the answer, and the people they speak of are Israel, who were brought out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: took hold of: clung to, attached themselves firmly to
decisions.reason: The verb means to grasp and hold on tight. Israel let go of the LORD and held fast to other gods instead.

decisions.choice: disaster: calamity, harm that comes on them
decisions.reason: The word is often translated "evil", but here it means the trouble and ruin that the LORD brings as judgment, not moral wrong.

decisions.choice: ancestors; people will answer
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers", and name the speakers as "people", since "they" would be unclear. The closing double quote ends the LORD's speech that began in verse 3.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י מִקְצֵה֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־בָּנָ֥ה שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אֶת־שְׁנֵ֣י הַבָּתִּ֑ים אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was at [the] end of twenty years which built Solomon the two houses, the house of Yahweh and the house of the king,

en.L: And it happened at the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the two houses, the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the house of the king,
en.B: At the end of the twenty years it took Solomon to build the two houses, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house and the royal palace,
en.R: It took Solomon twenty years to build the two buildings, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple and the royal palace.

es.L: Y sucedió al cabo de veinte años, en que Salomón había edificado las dos casas, la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y la casa del rey,
es.B: Al cabo de los veinte años que Salomón tardó en edificar las dos casas, la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y el palacio real,
es.R: Salomón tardó veinte años en construir los dos edificios, el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y el palacio real.

fr.L: Et il arriva, au bout de vingt ans, pendant lesquels Salomon avait bâti les deux maisons, la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et la maison du roi,
fr.B: Au bout des vingt ans qu’il fallut à Salomon pour bâtir les deux maisons, la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et le palais royal,
fr.R: Salomon a mis vingt ans à construire les deux bâtiments, le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et le palais royal.

sw.L: Ikawa mwisho wa miaka ishirini, ambayo Sulemani aliijenga zile nyumba mbili, nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na nyumba ya mfalme,
sw.B: Mwisho wa miaka ishirini ambayo Sulemani alitumia kujenga nyumba zile mbili, nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na ikulu ya mfalme,

vi.B: Vào cuối hai mươi năm Sa-lô-môn xây hai ngôi nhà, là nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và cung điện của vua,
vi.R: Sa-lô-môn mất hai mươi năm để xây hai công trình là đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và cung điện của vua.

ko.L: 그리고 솔로몬이 두 집, 곧 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집과 왕의 집을 지은 이십 년이 끝났을 때에,
ko.B: 솔로몬이 두 건물, 곧 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집과 왕궁을 짓는 데 이십 년이 걸렸다.
ko.R: 솔로몬이 두 건물, 곧 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전과 왕궁을 짓는 데 이십 년이 걸렸다.

decisions.choice: twenty years: seven for the temple and thirteen for the palace
decisions.reason: The temple took seven years (6:38) and the palace thirteen (7:1), so the whole building program lasted twenty years.

decisions.choice: a time clause that runs on into verse 11
decisions.reason: The sentence begins here and reaches its main statement in verse 11, "then King Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities"; the first half of verse 11 is an aside about Hiram.

decisions.choice: It took Solomon twenty years ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes the time clause a sentence of its own, and gives the main statement in verse 11 with "So".

source.text: חִירָ֣ם מֶֽלֶךְ־צֹ֠ר נִשָּׂ֨א אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה בַּעֲצֵי֩ אֲרָזִ֨ים וּבַעֲצֵ֧י בְרוֹשִׁ֛ים וּבַזָּהָ֖ב לְכָל־חֶפְצ֑וֹ אָ֡ז יִתֵּן֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה לְחִירָם֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים עִ֔יר בְּאֶ֖רֶץ הַגָּלִֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: Hiram king of Tyre had supplied Solomon with timber of cedars and with timber of cypresses and with gold according to all his desire, then gave the king Solomon to Hiram twenty cities in [the] land of the Galilee.

en.L: Hiram king of Tyre had supplied Solomon with cedar timber and with cypress timber and with gold, as much as he desired; then King Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
en.B: since Hiram king of Tyre had supplied Solomon with all the cedar and cypress timber and gold he wanted, King Solomon gave Hiram twenty towns in the region of Galilee.
en.R: Hiram, the king of Tyre, had given Solomon all the cedar and cypress wood and gold he wanted. So King Solomon gave Hiram twenty towns in the area of Galilee.

es.L: como Hiram, rey de Tiro, había provisto a Salomón de madera de cedro y de madera de ciprés y de oro, todo lo que quiso, el rey Salomón dio entonces a Hiram veinte ciudades en la tierra de Galilea.
es.B: como Hiram, rey de Tiro, le había proporcionado a Salomón toda la madera de cedro y de ciprés y todo el oro que quiso, el rey Salomón le dio a Hiram veinte pueblos en la región de Galilea.
es.R: Hiram, el rey de Tiro, le había dado a Salomón toda la madera de cedro y de ciprés y todo el oro que quiso. Por eso el rey Salomón le dio a Hiram veinte pueblos en la zona de Galilea.

fr.L: Hiram, roi de Tyr, avait fourni à Salomon du bois de cèdre, et du bois de cyprès, et de l’or, autant qu’il en désirait ; alors le roi Salomon donna à Hiram vingt villes dans le pays de Galilée.
fr.B: comme Hiram, roi de Tyr, avait fourni à Salomon tout le bois de cèdre et de cyprès et tout l’or qu’il voulait, le roi Salomon donna à Hiram vingt villes dans la région de Galilée.
fr.R: Hiram, le roi de Tyr, avait donné à Salomon tout le bois de cèdre et de cyprès et tout l’or qu’il voulait. Alors le roi Salomon a donné à Hiram vingt villes dans la région de Galilée.

sw.L: Hiramu mfalme wa Tiro alikuwa amempatia Sulemani mbao za mierezi na mbao za misunobari na dhahabu, kwa kadiri ya yote aliyotaka; ndipo mfalme Sulemani akampa Hiramu miji ishirini katika nchi ya Galilaya.
sw.B: kwa kuwa Hiramu mfalme wa Tiro alikuwa amempatia Sulemani mbao zote za mierezi na misunobari na dhahabu aliyotaka, mfalme Sulemani alimpa Hiramu miji ishirini katika eneo la Galilaya.
sw.R: Hiramu, mfalme wa Tiro, alikuwa amempa Sulemani mbao zote za mierezi na misunobari na dhahabu aliyotaka. Basi mfalme Sulemani akampa Hiramu miji ishirini katika eneo la Galilaya.

vi.L: Hi-ram vua Ty-rơ đã cung cấp cho Sa-lô-môn gỗ bá hương, gỗ bách và vàng, theo mọi điều vua muốn; bấy giờ vua Sa-lô-môn ban cho Hi-ram hai mươi thành trong xứ Ga-li-lê.

vi.R: Hi-ram, vua Ty-rơ, đã cung cấp cho Sa-lô-môn tất cả gỗ bá hương, gỗ bách và vàng vua cần. Vì vậy vua Sa-lô-môn tặng Hi-ram hai mươi thành trong vùng Ga-li-lê.

ko.L: 두로 왕 히람은 솔로몬이 원하는 대로 백향목 재목과 잣나무 재목과 금을 솔로몬에게 대 주었다. 그때 솔로몬 왕이 히람에게 갈릴리 땅에 있는 성읍 스무 개를 주었다.
ko.B: 두로 왕 히람은 솔로몬이 원하는 만큼 백향목과 잣나무 재목과 금을 대 주었다. 그래서 솔로몬 왕은 히람에게 갈릴리 지방에 있는 성읍 스무 개를 주었다.
ko.R: 두로 왕 히람은 솔로몬이 원하는 만큼 백향목과 잣나무와 금을 주었다. 그래서 솔로몬 왕은 히람에게 갈릴리 지역에 있는 성읍 스무 개를 주었다.

decisions.choice: Hiram had supplied Solomon: the agreement of chapter 5
decisions.reason: Hiram sent cedar and cypress from Lebanon in return for wheat and oil (5:22-25), and the two kings made a treaty (5:26). The gold is not mentioned there; it may be the gold of verse 14.

decisions.choice: cypress: a tall conifer of Lebanon
decisions.reason: The tree is not identified with certainty; it may be a cypress, a juniper or a fir. It is named beside cedar as fine building timber (5:22; 6:15, 34).

decisions.choice: twenty cities in the land of Galilee: towns in the north, on the border of Tyre's territory
decisions.reason: Galilee here is the district of northern Israel next to Phoenicia, in the area given to Asher (Joshua 19:24-31). "Cities" can name small walled towns or villages.

decisions.choice: then ... gave: the payment came when the building was done
decisions.reason: "Then" ties the gift to the end of the twenty years in verse 10. Whether the towns were a payment for Hiram's supplies or a pledge for them is not said.

decisions.choice: towns; region (Balanced), area (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Towns" suits places of this size better than "cities", and "region" or "area" shows that "the land of Galilee" is a district, not a country. Balanced begins with "since" to carry on the sentence from verse 10.

records.literal_gloss: And came out Hiram from Tyre to see the cities which had given to him Solomon, and not they were right in his eyes.

en.L: And Hiram came out from Tyre to see the cities that Solomon had given him, and they were not right in his eyes.
en.B: But when Hiram came from Tyre to see the towns Solomon had given him, they did not please him.
en.R: Hiram went from Tyre to look at the towns Solomon had given him. But he did not like them.

es.L: Y salió Hiram de Tiro para ver las ciudades que Salomón le había dado, y no le parecieron bien.
es.B: Pero cuando Hiram vino de Tiro a ver los pueblos que Salomón le había dado, no le gustaron.
es.R: Hiram fue desde Tiro a ver los pueblos que Salomón le había dado. Pero no le gustaron.

fr.L: Et Hiram sortit de Tyr pour voir les villes que Salomon lui avait données, et elles ne furent pas droites à ses yeux.
fr.B: Mais quand Hiram vint de Tyr pour voir les villes que Salomon lui avait données, elles ne lui plurent pas.
fr.R: Hiram est venu de Tyr pour voir les villes que Salomon lui avait données. Mais elles ne lui ont pas plu.

sw.L: Hiramu akatoka Tiro kuiona miji ambayo Sulemani alimpa, nayo haikuwa sawa machoni pake.
sw.B: Lakini Hiramu alipotoka Tiro kuja kuiona miji ambayo Sulemani alimpa, haikumpendeza.
sw.R: Hiramu alikwenda kutoka Tiro kuitazama miji ambayo Sulemani alimpa. Lakini hakuipenda.

vi.L: Hi-ram từ Ty-rơ ra xem các thành Sa-lô-môn đã ban cho mình, nhưng chúng không đẹp mắt ông.
vi.B: Nhưng khi Hi-ram từ Ty-rơ đến xem các thành Sa-lô-môn đã ban cho mình, ông không vừa ý.
vi.R: Hi-ram từ Ty-rơ đến xem các thành Sa-lô-môn đã tặng mình. Nhưng ông không thích chúng.

ko.L: 그리고 히람이 솔로몬이 자기에게 준 성읍들을 보려고 두로에서 나왔는데, 그것들이 그의 눈에 좋지 않았다.
ko.B: 그러나 히람이 솔로몬에게서 받은 성읍들을 보려고 두로에서 왔을 때, 그 성읍들이 마음에 들지 않았다.
ko.R: 히람은 솔로몬이 준 성읍들을 보려고 두로에서 갔다. 그러나 그 성읍들이 마음에 들지 않았다.

decisions.choice: they were not right in his eyes: they did not please him
decisions.reason: "Right in someone's eyes" means acceptable or pleasing to that person. Hiram thought the towns a poor return.

decisions.choice: did not please him (Balanced); did not like them (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom in plain words.

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מָ֚ה הֶעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥תָּה לִּ֖י אָחִ֑י וַיִּקְרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֶ֣רֶץ כָּב֔וּל עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he said, What [are] the cities these which you have given to me, my brother? And he called them land of Cabul until the day this.

en.L: And he said, "What [are] these cities that you have given me, my brother?" And he called them the land of Cabul, to this day.
en.B: He said, "What kind of towns are these you have given me, my brother?" So they have been called the land of Cabul to this day.
en.R: He said, "My brother, what kind of towns are these that you have given me?" So that area was called the land of Cabul, which sounds like "good for nothing". It is still called that to this day.

es.L: Y dijo: «¿Qué ciudades [son] estas que me has dado, hermano mío?». Y las llamó tierra de Cabul, hasta el día de hoy.
es.B: Dijo: «¿Qué clase de pueblos son estos que me has dado, hermano mío?». Por eso se les ha llamado tierra de Cabul hasta el día de hoy.
es.R: Dijo: «Hermano mío, ¿qué clase de pueblos son estos que me has dado?». Por eso esa zona se llamó tierra de Cabul, que suena como “no vale nada”. Así se llama todavía hasta el día de hoy.

fr.L: Et il dit : « Que [sont] ces villes que tu m’as données, mon frère ? » Et il les appela pays de Kaboul, jusqu’à ce jour.
fr.B: Il dit : « Que sont donc ces villes que tu m’as données, mon frère ? » Et on les a appelées pays de Kaboul jusqu’à aujourd’hui.
fr.R: Il a dit : « Mon frère, qu’est-ce que c’est que ces villes que tu m’as données ? » C’est pour cela que cette région a été appelée le pays de Kaboul, ce qui ressemble à « bon à rien ». On l’appelle encore ainsi jusqu’à aujourd’hui.

sw.L: Akasema, "Ni miji gani hii uliyonipa, ndugu yangu?" Akaiita nchi ya Kabuli, mpaka siku hii ya leo.
sw.B: Akasema, "Ni miji ya namna gani hii uliyonipa, ndugu yangu?" Hivyo imeitwa nchi ya Kabuli mpaka leo.
sw.R: Akasema, "Ndugu yangu, ni miji ya namna gani hii uliyonipa?" Basi eneo hilo likaitwa nchi ya Kabuli, jina linalosikika kama "isiyofaa kitu". Linaitwa hivyo mpaka leo.

vi.L: Ông nói: "Hỡi người anh em của tôi, những thành ông đã ban cho tôi là gì vậy?" Ông gọi chúng là xứ Ca-bun cho đến ngày nay.
vi.B: Ông nói: "Hỡi người anh em, ông đã cho tôi những thành gì thế này?" Vì vậy chúng được gọi là xứ Ca-bun cho đến ngày nay.
vi.R: Ông nói: "Người anh em của tôi ơi, ông cho tôi những thành gì thế này?" Vì vậy vùng ấy được gọi là xứ Ca-bun, nghe giống như "chẳng ra gì". Cho đến ngày nay vùng ấy vẫn được gọi như vậy.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 말했다. "내 형제여, 당신이 내게 준 이 성읍들이 무엇입니까?" 그리고 그는 그것들을 가불 땅이라고 불렀다. 오늘날까지 [그렇게 불린다].
ko.B: 히람이 말했다. "내 형제여, 왕께서 내게 주신 이 성읍들이 도대체 무엇입니까?" 그래서 그곳은 오늘날까지 가불 땅이라고 불린다.
ko.R: 히람이 말했다. "내 형제여, 왕께서 내게 주신 성읍들이 이게 뭡니까?" 그래서 그 지역은 가불 땅이라고 불리게 되었다. 가불은 '쓸모없다'는 말처럼 들린다. 그곳은 오늘날까지 그렇게 불린다.

decisions.choice: what are these cities: a scornful question
decisions.reason: Hiram is not asking for information; he is expressing his low opinion of the gift.

decisions.choice: my brother: the address of an ally of equal rank
decisions.reason: Kings bound by a treaty called each other "brother" (compare 20:32-33). Solomon and Hiram had made such a treaty (5:26), so the word is polite even while Hiram complains.

decisions.choice: Cabul: a name that sounds like "as nothing"
decisions.reason: The name was understood as a play on words: in Hebrew it sounds like "like nothing" or "as good as nothing", which fits Hiram's complaint. The exact sense of the wordplay is not certain. There was a town Cabul in the territory of Asher (Joshua 19:27), so the name may be older than the story and taken up as a joke.

decisions.choice: he called them ... to this day: the name was still used in the writer's own day
decisions.reason: "He called" may mean Hiram or may be impersonal, "they were called". "To this day" means the time of the writer, as at 8:8.

decisions.choice: they have been called (Balanced); that area was called (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave open who gave the name, as the impersonal sense allows.

decisions.choice: which sounds like "good for nothing"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wordplay so the reader can see why the name stuck. The exact sense of the pun is uncertain, but its point, that the towns were worth little, is clear from Hiram's words.

decisions.choice: "que suena como “no vale nada”" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English Readable (r-en-2): Readable explains the play on the name Cabul.

decisions.choice: "người anh em" for Hiram's "my brother"
decisions.reason: Between allied kings "brother" is a treaty word, not a family tie; Vietnamese "người anh em" keeps it without saying who is older.

decisions.choice: "내 형제여" with 합쇼체, as between allied kings
decisions.reason: The address of an equal ally; Korean keeps the formal style of the letters in chapter 5, so the scorn sits in the words, not the register.

vi.R: Hi-ram đã gửi cho vua Sa-lô-môn {{units:khoảng 4.080 kg|120 ta-lâng}} vàng.

ko.R: 히람은 솔로몬 왕에게 금을 {{units:4,080킬로그램쯤|백이십 달란트}}나 보냈었다.

decisions.choice: had sent: the gold Hiram had already supplied
decisions.reason: The verb can be read as "had sent", looking back to the gold of verse 11, or as "then sent", a payment for the towns despite his complaint. The first fits the flow from verse 11 better.

decisions.choice: talent: the largest weight, about 75 pounds
decisions.reason: A talent was 3,000 shekels. 120 talents of gold is about 9,000 pounds, or about 4 1/2 tons.

decisions.choice: about 9,000 pounds (with 120 talents as the setting)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern weight, with the talent as the alternative, as for every measure.

decisions.choice: {{units:unos 4 080 kilos|ciento veinte talentos}}
decisions.reason: The talent is counted at 34 kg, as the Kings terms note sets; Balanced and Readable convert, as the English does (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: karibu kilo 4,080 (talanta as the alternative)
decisions.reason: Swahili gives the weight in kilograms (a talent about 34 kg), with the talents as the alternative, where the English converts to pounds.

decisions.choice: "khoảng 4.080 kg" (default); "120 ta-lâng" (alternative)
decisions.reason: Metric by default, with the talent of 34 kg the terms note sets, as in the Vietnamese Samuel; Literal keeps the talents.

decisions.choice: Kilograms by default (talent 34 kg), "달란트" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As the Kings and Chronicles terms note's metric values; Literal keeps the talents.
